#  acceptance fixtures and runner contract

The frozen category oracle is generated by `generate.py`, reading committed project
text under `docs/user/cli`, never edi's category functions. The field sets are
transcribed from diffraction-lib `0ffba46f` class declarations and the accepted
packet §2b's explicitly declared divergences. The file records each experiment's
SHA-256. It includes every committed CLI project, including both scan fixtures.

The background declarations extend the category and displayed-value oracles with the registered
CeCoAl/POLARIS Chebyshev, CeO2/PEARL polynomial and LaB6/ECHIDNA TCH+FCJ projects.
Regenerate both with `python tests/fixtures/e04_t1/generate.py` and
`python tests/fixtures/e04_t1/generate_display.py`. Their values and hashes come
from the committed `.edi` files; CeCoAl's `P m m a` display identity is ITA 51,
orthorhombic (also independently frozen in crysta's space-group oracle).

The app acceptance tier is `tests/unit/app`. Build its `test_*.cpp` support sources
into the Qt Quick Test runner (AUTOMOC), linked to the same registered `edi.app`
module and engine setup the production host uses. Run its `tst_*.qml` files with
Qt Quick Test. The support module is test-only: never link it into `edi_app`.
`app-build` builds the runner; `app-test` runs it and refuses zero executed cases.

The screenshot comparator acceptance cases run the production
`edi_app_ui_compare --actual DIR --expected DIR --diff DIR`. Set
`EDI_APP_UI_COMPARE` if the built executable is outside `build/app/app` or
`build/app`. The expected set is ONE platform-independent baseline per the owner
record of 2026-09-27, labelled as an edi regression pin. Its look still needs the
side-by-side review of the owner originals.

The owner-amended plan §5b (2026-09-27) replaces the original pixel-fraction
metric with luminance SSIM: 8×8 windows, aggregated over 32×32 tiles; minimum tile
0.90, whole image 0.98. The synthetic comparator inputs exercise identical
images, small luminance changes, a mean-only failure and a tile-only failure, plus
missing and differently sized images. Constant-field SSIM has a closed form;
its provenance is the comment beside the cases. A single pixel is no longer
claimed to fail. The baseline includes the loaded-experiment state 26 and the
final plan amendment's X-ray state 27. The 2026-09-28 owner direction adds
About as state 28. State 25 captures the stable TOF report (`25-report-tof`);
the monospace Text-tab captures remain states 09, 23 and 24. The gate requires
their explicit filenames as well as the complete numbered range 01 through 28.

The calculated Text in `23-experiment-text` and three report Text captures
(`t2-05`, `t2-09`, `t2-10`) no longer contains the retired source commit and
input fingerprint lines. The app acceptance case I8 compares Text with the
separately generated Python writer reference at this build. Writer bytes,
including the absence of those lines, column declarations, row order, spacing,
measured values and current structure categories, remain exact. Only calculated
numeric columns in `_data`, `_refln`, `_expanded_atom_site.cartn_x/y/z`, and
`_geom_bond.distance` admit a 1e-12 relative or absolute difference: the same
calculation can finish with different last digits across operating systems;
material numeric changes fail. Structure identifiers, labels, symmetry codes,
fractional coordinates, occupancies, row order and spacing remain byte-exact.
Regenerate the reference JSON
with `generate_reference.py` when calculation output or the saved schema changes.
The  refreeze used edi `2851a96` against crysta `19a91fb5`; its generated
reference is in `/tmp/-e04-reference/reference.json` and the run log is
`<author-runs>/-tests-triage/e04.log`. Its axes and calculated arrays stayed
byte-identical; the structure texts gained schema 4 and the four computed
categories, while experiment texts lost only the two retired identity lines.

The runtime escape driver uses `EDI_APP_TEST_RUNNER` (default
`build/app/app/edi_app_tests`) and `EDI_APP_QMLLINT` (default the app environment's
qmllint). `QML_IMPORT_PATH` must include the same generated modules the production
lint uses. The test runner must forward the standard Qt Quick Test `-input` and
`-o` arguments. Negative fixture names deliberately lack the `tst_` prefix, so the
normal app suite does not collect intentionally failing cases.

`generate_reference.py OUTPUT` supplies live, separate-surface wiring references
using unchanged Python calculation and save behavior. The runner receives the
output directory through `EDI_ACCEPTANCE_REFERENCE`; these are wiring references,
not independent physics goldens. No Python selector behavior change is expected
(owner clarification 2026-09-27).

The existing-project extension follows **all** ids in `docs/user/cli/projects.yml`
in registry order, including non-executing and offline entries. `generate.py`
freezes their metadata, structure summaries and file hashes from project text.
The live reference generator also copies diamond/DREAM into an unlisted directory
with spaces; it retains the absent `_experiment_type` declarations.

For real Examples clicks, the Project page exposes these stable demo targets:
`group.examples` (expand the group), `examples.list` (the gui-components TableView,
which is a ListView), and `examples.open.<registry-id>` (each row's open control).
The gate scrolls the base view to each row, clicks the control and visits every
workflow page with Qt warnings fatal. Text panes and the report must render the
loaded data. Whole-directory opening retains inferred types; the separate
add-experiment tests continue to require every declared type axis.

The later owner records (conductor drives 10–11) extend this contract. Generate
their small inputs with `generate_amendments.py`: LiF structure/experiment values
come from the committed  fixture, with synthetic observations; the
editable project copies LBCO with a declared custom neutron length. These inputs
are selector/editing witnesses, not physics goldens. The additional legacy
minimizer spelling exercises the same library warning path as scan-3f. The probe
observes `std::cerr` in an independent `edi::load_project` call; the app must show
the diagnostic, display the effective `crysta` minimizer, and preserve the stored
legacy token in Text. Qt warnings are still fatal.
If the visible warning is modal, its close control is `warning.dismiss`.

Library-settable properties and table roles are writable through the typed
view-model and the visible editor. `StructureViewModel.scatteringLengths` is a
typed model with `typeSymbol` and `lengthFm` roles. The stable UI targets added
for this coverage are `group.<category_id>` on every category group (the group header/container, with its
content as descendants), `spaceGroup.nameHM`, `spaceGroup.coordSystemCode`,
`atomSite.label.<row>`, `atomSite.typeSymbol.<row>`, `atomSite.adpIso.<row>`,
`scatteringLength.lengthFm.<row>`, `background.position.<row>`,
`excludedRegion.start.<row>`, `excludedRegion.end.<row>`,
`preferredOrientation.indexH.<row>` / `indexK` / `indexL`,
`minimizer.maxIterations`, `minimizer.chiSquareTolerance`, and `peak.<edi_leaf>`.
Targets for editable scalars/columns are the actual text editor (`readOnly ==
false`); indices start at zero. The selectors `background.type` and
`scatteringSource.<edi_leaf>` expose their typed option models with token roles.
Labels may be human-readable; the selected value must represent the stored token.
Asymmetry fields and cutoff are descendants of the peak group, and ADP columns
are descendants of atom sites; neither creates a separate group.
The separate block-list actions use `group.structures` and `group.experiments`
if they are rendered as groups. Every visible category group is inventoried
across Basic and Extras, including duplicates and unrecognised category ids.

The final Report direction supersedes the interim placeholder. `report.text`
is a standard QML Text/TextArea with RichText formatting. It presents Crystal
data (structure names, space group, cell lengths and angles), Data collection
(experiment names, measured ranges and point counts), and Refinement
(effective minimizer). Expectations are frozen
from the committed input files, including analysis blocks; no app output is an
oracle. The content contains no script, plot or embedded browser. No WebEngine
or WebView module may be imported or linked.

The displayed-value extension (`generate_display.py`, `display_oracle.js`)
freezes every CLI project's structures and experiments plus the X-ray, editable
and warning witnesses. Its inputs are hashed `.edi` bytes. It covers the four
disabled experiment axes, crystal system, space-group number/name/code, every
measured-range field, all scan fields, and the calculation/minimization engine
labels. The existing Text and Report gates continue to check native text views.
Parameter-table range labels additionally exercise the packet's bounded,
half-bounded and unbounded seam witnesses.

The expected IT number is the International Tables identity of the file's
Hermann–Mauguin name; an explicit `_space_group.it_number` must agree. In
particular, the frozen `cosio-d20_start-1` input names `P n m a` without storing
the number, whereas `cosio-d20_scan-324f` explicitly stores `62`. Both display
`62`; no value is harvested from the app or its writer. Legacy experiment
declarations follow the accepted directory-loader defaults (packet P1).

The gate observes ComboBox's native content-item text and the native TextInput
text of fields, including visibility, opacity and glyph colour. Model/options,
`currentIndex`, `fieldValue` and `displayText` are not display oracles. Deliberate
blank/wrong content with a correct model/index, hidden text and invisible glyphs
must fail the same observer. Disabled actions that do not present loaded data
(save, undo, fitting and export) remain under the existing workflow contract.

 re-freezes the wiring regression JSON through `generate_reference.py`
against edi `e6579e64` and pinned crysta SDK `build-417ffe01`. The generated
axes and calculated arrays are unchanged; exactly the three experiment texts
gain `_calculator.type crysta` and its block separator. All other saved-text

Setting fields omitted from an input now display the resolved reference default.
`generate_display.py` freezes the corpus defaults from unmodified CrySPY
`b37f9f3148d2771c6d84ee91f57331676d93746f`,
`function_2_space_group.get_default_it_coordinate_system_code_by_it_number`.
Explicit file codes retain priority. The CW instrument inventory also retains
the FullProf La11B6 corpus's displacement and transparency fields, mapped from
`SyCos` and `SySin` in that case's `PROVENANCE.md`. Neither generator imports edi.
The optional TOF Gaussian/Lorentz size and strain terms use the zero defaults
in CrySPY's `powder_diffraction_tof.py` (`calc_sigma`, `calc_sigma_gamma`).
Only absent optional terms receive these defaults; all declared values and
free flags remain the committed input values.
